h1: The 5 Best 85-Inch TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 TVs at 85 inches scored on panel type, refresh rate, smart platform and value, from Mini-LED to entry-level 4K LED.
summary: The Hisense 85-inch U7 is the best 85-inch TV for most buyers: Mini-LED backlighting, a 165Hz panel and Google TV. The Samsung M80H is the Mini-LED pick for people who prefer Samsung's ecosystem. The Samsung Q8F steps down to QLED at lower cost, and the Samsung U8000H and INSIGNIA F50 are the budget 4K sets for big-screen buyers who accept plainer picture technology.
intro: At 85 inches, panel technology stops being a spec-sheet footnote and becomes the whole decision. Every flaw scales with the screen: a basic LED backlight with few dimming zones leaves gray, hazy blacks across a surface larger than most coffee tables, and a bright window in the room turns it into a mirror. Buying by price alone gets you size, not picture.

So we ranked five 85-inch sets by backlight type first, then refresh rate, smart platform and cost. We reviewed spec sheets and owner feedback for Mini-LED, QLED and standard LED designs, and scored each on the Primea framework. Seat distance matters too: an 85-inch screen needs roughly 9 to 12 feet to fill your view without showing pixel structure on lower-grade panels.

products.name: Hisense 85" U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K UHD Best Premium Gaming Smart Google
products.verdict: Mini-LED backlighting, a 165Hz panel and Google TV at 85 inches.
products.description:
Hisense's 85-inch U7 pairs Mini-LED backlighting with a 165Hz panel and a Google TV platform. Mini-LED packs far more small backlight zones behind the panel than standard LED, so bright highlights and dark areas can sit side by side without a washed-out glow.

It leads because it is the only set here that combines Mini-LED with a gaming-grade 165Hz refresh rate. Against the Samsung M80H, which also uses Mini-LED, the U7 adds the high refresh figure, a spec that matters for console and PC gamers. Against the QLED Samsungs below, you get a more advanced backlight.

Buy it for movies and gaming in a room you can darken. The caveat is that the listing publishes no brightness figure, so a sunlit living room is the scenario where you should verify output before ordering.
products.idealFor: Gamers and film fans in a controllable-light room.
products.skipIf: You want a Samsung ecosystem or a very bright-room set.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class M80H Series
products.verdict: Samsung's Mini-LED at 85 inches, without a stated gaming refresh rate.
products.description:
The M80H is Samsung's 85-inch Mini-LED set. Mini-LED backlighting is the reason to look at the M80H instead of the cheaper QLED models: more backlight zones mean more control over contrast on a very large panel.

It takes second place behind the Hisense because the Hisense lists 165Hz, whereas the M80H listing does not state a refresh rate. Against the Q8F, the M80H has the stronger backlight technology, though it is less clear on the extras. For a buyer who wants Samsung's smart platform and a premium backlight, this is the step above the QLED line.

Buy it for a bright-ish living room where contrast matters. The caveat is the listing's thin detail: no refresh rate, no brightness, so confirm those against Samsung's spec page before buying.
products.idealFor: Samsung buyers who want a Mini-LED step up from QLED.
products.skipIf: A listed 165Hz gaming refresh rate is a must-have.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class QLED Q8F 4K UHD Smart TV (2025 Model) Q4 AI
products.verdict: A 2025 QLED 4K with Samsung's AI processor, below the Mini-LED sets.
products.description:
The Q8F is a 2025 85-inch QLED 4K Smart TV from Samsung, with a Q4 AI processor named in the title. QLED uses a quantum-dot layer to widen the color range, which is a visible gain over a plain LED set when the screen is this large.

It ranks third because Mini-LED handles contrast better than QLED alone, which is why the Hisense and M80H sit above it. Against the plain Crystal UHD below, the Q8F adds the quantum-dot layer and a named AI processor, which is your reason to pay the premium. You lose Mini-LED zones, but you keep strong color.

Buy it for movie-night color at 85 inches when Mini-LED stretches the budget. Its weak spot is paperwork: refresh rate and HDR detail are missing, so confirm gaming needs elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Movie watchers who value color and want a recent Samsung model.
products.skipIf: Deep blacks are your top priority in a dark room.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class U8000H Series Crystal UHD
products.verdict: A Crystal UHD 4K Samsung for those who want size over picture technology.
products.description:
The U8000H is Samsung's 85-inch Crystal UHD 4K set. Crystal UHD is Samsung's standard LED tier, without the quantum-dot layer of QLED or the dense zones of Mini-LED.

It ranks fourth because the picture technology is the plainest of the Samsungs. Against the Q8F, you give up the QLED color range, and the price saving is the reason to choose it. Against the INSIGNIA below, it keeps a recognized brand and platform for a similar size.

Buy it for a bright family room where you want a very large 4K screen on a budget. The caveat is dark-room performance: standard LED without local dimming tends to show grayer blacks than the sets above.
products.idealFor: Casual family viewing in a bright living room.
products.skipIf: You watch films in a dark room or want gaming features.

products.name: INSIGNIA 85" Class F50 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV with Alexa
products.verdict: The entry ticket to 85 inches, with Fire TV and Alexa built in.
products.description:
INSIGNIA's F50 is an 85-inch LED 4K UHD set running Fire TV with Alexa voice control. It lists in the $500 and up bracket alongside the rest, but its panel technology is the most basic.

It ranks last because the specs show only LED and 4K, with no Mini-LED, no quantum-dot layer and no refresh figure. Against the Samsung U8000H, the INSIGNIA's selling point is the Fire TV platform, which suits households already using Alexa. Both are plain LED, so the brand and smart platform decide.

Buy it if you want the largest screen for the least money, and you live in the Amazon ecosystem. The caveat is picture quality: a big LED with limited dimming can look flat in a dark room.
products.idealFor: Alexa households who want the biggest screen for the least spend.
products.skipIf: Picture quality or gaming performance matters most.

methodology.title: Backlight technology
methodology.description: Mini-LED, QLED and standard LED differ in contrast control, and at 85 inches that gap is large, so we weighted panel type most.

methodology.title: Refresh rate
methodology.description: A listed 165Hz panel scored above unspecified rates, since gamers need the figure confirmed.

methodology.title: Smart platform
methodology.description: Google TV, Fire TV and Samsung's platform differ in apps and voice control, so we considered which suits each buyer.

methodology.title: Information quality
methodology.description: Listings that publish model year, processor and panel type scored higher than those that leave it blank.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: We compared each set's panel technology against its price bracket, since cost per inch alone hides weak backlights.

whatMatters.detail: Mini-LED uses many small backlight zones to dim dark areas independently, giving better contrast than QLED or standard LED on the same panel. At 85 inches, the difference is obvious in dark scenes. Look for the words Mini-LED in the title, and treat unlabeled LED as the basic tier.

QLED adds a quantum-dot layer that widens the color range, making reds and greens richer than a plain LED. It does not improve black levels the way local dimming does. Check for QLED in the title, as on the Q8F, if color matters.

Hertz counts how often the panel redraws the image each second. A listed 165Hz, as on the Hisense U7, suits fast gameplay on a PC or console. Most film and TV is slower. If a listing does not state it, assume a standard rate.

An 85-inch screen needs room: roughly 9 to 12 feet gives a comfortable field of view. Closer than that, lower-grade panels show their structure. Measure the distance from your sofa to the wall before ordering, and check that the delivery path through doorways is wide enough.

The platform controls apps, search and voice. The Hisense runs Google TV, the INSIGNIA runs Fire TV with Alexa, and Samsung uses its own. Choose the one that matches the assistant and accounts you already use, since changing later means a separate streaming box.

faq.q: Will an 85-inch TV fit through my door?
faq.a: Measure the doorway, stairwell and any turns before ordering. The Hisense U7, Samsung M80H and the others ship in large cartons, and wall-mounting an 85-inch panel usually needs a second person and a rated bracket.

faq.q: Is the Hisense U7 good for PlayStation or Xbox?
faq.a: It lists 165Hz, which is the highest refresh rate in this ranking and suits console and PC gaming. The Samsung sets do not state a refresh rate on their listings, so check Samsung's spec page before buying for gaming.

faq.q: Is the Q8F worth it over the U8000H?
faq.a: Pay the premium if color matters. The Q8F adds the quantum-dot layer, the 2025 model year and the Q4 AI processor, while the U8000H is a standard Crystal UHD LED set. In a bright room the gap narrows.

faq.q: Do I need to mount an 85-inch TV?
faq.a: Many owners use the included stand on a wide, solid console, but check that the stand feet fit your furniture. The INSIGNIA F50 and Samsung sets all need a wide surface, so measure before assuming it will sit on your current unit.

faq.q: How do I reduce glare on a large panel?
faq.a: Place the Samsung or Hisense away from windows, use blinds in the afternoon, and avoid lamps behind your seat. Glare is more noticeable on a big screen, so a Mini-LED set helps only if the room is not over-lit.

faq.q: Does the INSIGNIA F50 work with Alexa?
faq.a: Yes, the title lists Fire TV with Alexa. It suits a household already using Echo devices, but it is a plain LED panel, so expect weaker dark-room contrast than the Hisense U7 or Samsung M80H.

finalTake: For most buyers the Hisense 85-inch U7 is the best 85-inch TV: Mini-LED backlighting, a 165Hz panel and Google TV. If you prefer Samsung, the M80H is the Mini-LED way in. For color on a tighter budget, the Q8F is the pick, and the INSIGNIA F50 is the cheapest route to a very large screen if picture technology is secondary.
